draft: The sky over Mexico City is a blend of blue smog and amber haze. The streets are bustling but arguments occur at markets and marches. Credit apps and gig economy jobs are advertised, while mutual aid groups distribute flyers in plazas. Water rationing signs hang on walls as neighbors share updates on their rainwater tanks with optimism. Adaptation to shifting rains and heat is evident, alongside surveillance drones, cooperatives, and creeping debt. Tensions are palpable, held at bay by negotiation tables and monitoring, while environmental and social disasters loom. Life continues, displaying resilience and adaptability amidst challenges in an increasingly complex world.

The streets bustle with friendly faces, as people go about their lives without much interference from the government. Civic ministries are open to all, offering help and support freely. Mutual aid groups flourish at local markets, sharing goods and labor in harmony.

There's an easy breath of fresh air as you look out your window, crisp and clean despite a growing urban sprawl. Canals snake through neighborhoods, water levels carefully monitored by hydrologists who work with the community to manage resources sustainably.

While there are some obvious signs of inequality—like shiny new co-ops next to crumbling apartment blocks—the overall mood is one of cautious optimism. People seem hopeful that their collective efforts can build a better world together.
